default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-308.title: Flat-channel regression stretch fade
E-308.hypothesis: When the least-squares line through the last window's closes is nearly flat (its total rise is small next to the residual scatter), the market is a horizontal channel worked by liquidity providers; a close that stretches k residual sds off the line is a passing order the providers absorb, so fade back toward the line (no trend required, unlike the trend-dip of E-139).

E-309.title: Wide-box micro-break fade
E-309.hypothesis: If the last window's high-low box is already much wider than the same window usually is at this minute, the move inside it has spent the day traders' range; a further close beyond the box edge is a late chaser in an overextended window that the responsive side leans against, so fade it (window width regime, not the session-range schedule of E-267).

E-310.title: Bounce-regime big-bar fade
E-310.hypothesis: When today's recent one-bar returns are clearly negatively autocorrelated (each move is partly undone on the next bar), price changes are dominated by inventory-managing liquidity providers (Roll's bid-ask bounce at a larger scale); a bar of unusually large range in that regime is a transient push they unwind, so fade its direction.

E-311.title: Harami after a wide bar fade
E-311.hypothesis: A wide bar followed at once by a small bar inside it means the wide bar's aggressor got no follow-through: the next participants traded only within its range and the chasers who entered at its close are not being rewarded; their exits push price back, so fade the wide bar's direction (the opposite of following an inside-bar break, E-005).

E-312.title: Prior-close order-imbalance inventory fade
E-312.hypothesis: A one-sided volume imbalance in the last 30 minutes of yesterday (volume on up bars against down bars) left market makers holding the opposite inventory overnight; they unload it during today's first hours as liquidity traders arrive, so rallies after a buy-imbalance close are sold and dips after a sell-imbalance close are bought: fade early micro-breaks in that direction (signed volume, not yesterday's price push of E-152).

E-313.title: Red bars, rising lows
E-313.hypothesis: Several consecutive bars that close below their open yet each make a higher low show sellers hitting the bid into every bar's close while a passive buyer keeps raising the floor; the aggressive sellers are being absorbed without progress and the absorber wins, so buy (mirror: green bars with lower highs, sell).

E-314.title: Flat-day open-magnet stretch fade
E-314.hypothesis: When the price was still near the session open a short while ago (the day has not chosen a side), a fast move to an unusually large distance from the open for this minute is a burst, not a trend: the open stays the day's reference for the two-sided participants, who fade it back toward the open.

E-315.title: Point-and-figure double-top break follow
E-315.hypothesis: Point-and-figure chartists (Dorsey) buy when an X column rises above the previous X column's top and sell when an O column falls below the previous O column's bottom; their simultaneous orders and the stops of the counter side resting at those columns push the first boxes of the break, so follow it (one signal per column; boxes as a fraction of the session open).

E-316.title: Stale-tape micro-break fade
E-316.hypothesis: A high share of bars that close exactly at the previous close (Lesmond's zero-return measure) means the price is pinned by thick resting orders and few informed trades arrive; a 15-minute break in such a stale tape is a small order poking through a refilling book, so fade it.

E-317.title: Clock-hour anchored VWAP stretch fade
E-317.hypothesis: Execution algorithms restart their schedules at each clock hour and benchmark the hour's VWAP; a close far outside that hour's volume-weighted band (k volume-weighted sds) is an impatient order ahead of the schedule, and the hour's benchmark traders fill against it, pulling price back to the hour's value (an hourly anchor, not the session VWAP of P-016).
